key_insight: A particle-based simulation shows that dense suspensions of granular spherocylinders exhibit a strong start-up viscosity spike and a steady rheology that depends systematically on particle concentration and aspect ratio.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict and tune the flow behavior of rod-shaped granular suspensions used in manufacturing and natural particulate systems, where viscosity and alignment affect processing and performance.
method: Tracks spherocylinder trajectories in simple shear flow.
Models short-range frictional contact and hydrodynamic interactions, including lubrication forces.
Uses dynamic timestep control for stable simulation of dense suspensions.
evidence_signal: The model is tested against limited experimental rheology data and reproduces trends in viscosity and microstructure across aspect ratios up to 20.
watch_item: The conclusions are constrained by the limited experimental dataset and may be sensitive to lubrication/contact modeling details for very dense or highly elongated particles.
paper_title: Rheology of dense suspensions of granular spherocylinders by particle-based simulation
